checkpoints: A Redis Sorted Set (ZSET) keeps its members ordered strictly by their numeric score inside an internal skip list, and ZREVRANGE simply walks that skip list from the high end to the low end.

Because ZREVRANGE has no concept of "recency" on its own, the order it returns is entirely determined by whatever value was written as the score at insert time — if that value doesn't represent time, the output doesn't represent time either.

In seedTimeline, the score passed to zadd is `rank`, a loop counter that increments by exactly 1 on every row processed, rather than `row.scoreMs`, the real epoch-millisecond timestamp already available on each post.
Because `rank` only reflects the order rows came back from `this.posts.find({ order: { scoreMs: "ASC" } })`, the ZSET ends up sorted by seed/insertion order rather than by true chronological recency.

A post that is genuinely newer (larger real scoreMs) but happens to be seeded earlier in the loop receives a smaller rank value than an older post seeded later, so it sinks below that older post when the feed is read back.

getCachedFeed itself is correct: zrevrange(key, 0, 19, "WITHSCORES") reading the 20 highest-score members in descending order is exactly the intended read pattern for this cache; the defect is confined entirely to the write side in seedTimeline.

The fix is a one-line change — replace `rank` with `row.scoreMs` in the zadd call — so that a larger score corresponds to a later epoch timestamp, and the already-correct ZREVRANGE read then produces strict recency order.

Correctness after the fix should be verified by seeding posts in a shuffled, non-chronological order and asserting the returned timeline is strictly descending by real scoreMs/createdAt; two posts sharing the exact same scoreMs fall back to lexicographic ordering on postId inside the skip list, a separate edge case worth noting but not the bug itself.
